entry.evidence: Paleoenvironmental reconstruction of the Mediterranean Basin at the end of the Messinian Salinity Crisis is contentious.

sequences.source_document: Published paper (PDF) with XML abstract and captions

steps.action: Frame the Stage 3 controversy as whether the Stage 3 depocentres were isolated or connected.
steps.quote: The nub of the controversy concerns the isolation or connectivity between the Stage 3 depocentres.

steps.action: Take from the literature two rival end-member hypotheses: endorheic lakes, or a Mediterranean filled enough by Atlantic, Paratethys and river water to link the sub-basins.
steps.quote: argues that Stage 3 sedimentation happened in endorheic lakes

steps.action: Argue that peripheral sub-basins such as the Piedmont Basin are a discriminating test location, because connectivity there requires a relatively full Mediterranean.
steps.quote: The sub-basins at the periphery of the Mediterranean system are a good location for testing the isolated/connected hypothesis

steps.action: Select the Pollenzo section, the only continuous exposure in the Piedmont Basin from the Stage 2 VVC to the basal Zanclean.
steps.quote: The Pollenzo section is the only locality in the Piedmont Basin where a continuous section from the Stage 2 VVC to the basal Zanclean

steps.action: Log the CSC in the field (February 2019) and collect 82 mudstone samples, plus four earlier samples from the interval now under water.
steps.quote: A total of 82 samples of mudstones were collected

steps.action: Set criteria for Sr-isotope material (not reworked, not diagenetically altered, cleaned of matrix, preferably low-Mg calcite) and select seven ostracod and foraminifer samples.
steps.quote: seven samples were selected for which sufficient ostracod

steps.action: Describe three lithological members (A subaqueous mudstones, B continental with fluvial conglomerates, C subaqueous mudstones) and two ostracod biofacies, Biofacies 2 being Paratethyan.
steps.quote: three members of the ~20 m-thick CSC can be recognized on the basis of lithological features

steps.action: Check that the ostracods are in situ, using multiple moult stages and articulated valves and, independently, the species' Paratethyan biogeographic range.
steps.quote: This observation further corroborates the in-situ character of the Biofacies 2 ostracods.

steps.action: Infer the reworked versus in-situ status of foraminifera (reworked: extinct and deep-dwelling taxa), nannofossils (<6% reworked; intact coccospheres in member C) and dinocysts (reworked in lower C, possibly in situ higher up).
steps.quote: Consequently, it is likely that the foraminifera are reworked.

steps.action: Measure 87Sr/86Sr on ostracod valves (0.708871 to 0.708746) and on one Zanclean foraminifer sample (0.709006) at the Bristol Isotope Group.
steps.quote: 87Sr/86Sr ratios from the CSC range from 0.708871 to 0.708746

steps.action: Infer the environment of each member from sedimentology and modern ostracod ecology: A shallow and brackish (salinity from Moncucco data), B an alluvial plain, C a shallow water body with fluctuating base level.
steps.quote: These findings therefore suggest that the shallow-water paleoenvironment depositing member A was typified by brackish conditions.

steps.action: Compare with modern low-salinity basins (Black Sea, Baltic, Adriatic, Thessaloniki Bay) and conclude that brackish ostracods and in-situ nannofossils can coexist, conditional on Wade and Bown (2006).
steps.quote: These studies of calcareous nannoplankton in modern, low salinity marine environments therefore do not preclude the coexistence

steps.action: Propose taphonomic and paleoecological criteria, instead of biostratigraphic markers (C. acutus, T. rugosus), for judging whether Stage 3 nannofossils are in situ.
steps.quote: We therefore suggest that taphonomic and paleoecological evidence, rather than biostratigraphic criteria, should be used

steps.action: Derive the endorheic-lake prediction: a lake filling Piedmont would have at least the Po River value before the Tanaro confluence (0.709187), assuming paleorivers resembled present-day rivers.
steps.quote: We consider the lowest 87Sr/86Sr ratio of the Po River before its confluence with the Tanaro River

steps.action: Compare the ostracod Sr ratios with the lake prediction and with coeval seawater: they lie below both.
steps.quote: This range of values, however, is substantially higher than the 87Sr/86Sr values measured on ostracods valves

steps.action: Vary the drainage auxiliary (a larger basin, or Po tributaries further east) and show that no Po value reaches the ostracod values.
steps.quote: Even if so, at no point beyond the present-day eastern margin of the Piedmont Basin the Po River attains 87Sr/86Sr values low enough

steps.action: Reject the endorheic lake fed by northern Italian rivers (e.g. Amadori et al., 2018) and require an external, low-87Sr/86Sr water source.
steps.quote: [...] not support the notion that the biota of the CSC inhabited an endorheic lake fed by northern Italian rivers

steps.action: Compare the Piedmont record with three SE Spanish marginal basins: in all four, the ostracod Sr ratios fall outside the endorheic-lake range.
steps.quote: none of the 87Sr/86Sr ratios measured on Biofacies 1 and 2 ostracods from four separated marginal basins overlap

steps.action: Keep the mixing of fluvial and Mediterranean water, which requires a Mediterranean full enough to reach Piedmont and dominated by non-marine water.
steps.quote: We therefore suggest that the 87Sr/86Sr Piedmont CSC data are also the consequence of mixed fluvial and Mediterranean input

steps.action: Refine the claim: the Sr decrease from Biofacies 1 to Biofacies 2 in upper member C reflects a growing Mediterranean contribution as the water deepened.
steps.quote: This decrease in 87Sr/86Sr in the upper part of member C is likely to reflect an enhanced contribution of Mediterranean water

steps.action: State catastrophic versus non-catastrophic rivals for the M/P transition; leave them undecided because the black layer is ambiguous.
steps.quote: The ambiguous nature of the topmost black layer at the M/P boundary (Fig. 2g) hampers the interpretation

steps.action: Derive the expectation that early Zanclean microfossils, deposited after full Atlantic replenishment, should carry ocean Sr ratios.
steps.quote: The 87Sr/86Sr of Early Zanclean microfossils should therefore be within error of ocean ratios.

steps.action: Compare FSS11 (0.709006) with the coeval ocean value (0.709024): the sample is measurably lower, a mismatch.
steps.quote: is close to, but analytically lower than the coeval ocean value

steps.action: Explain the mismatch as a delayed system response with residual non-marine Sr, using Topper et al. (2014) model results and similar records from Adana and Chelif.
steps.quote: We suggest that this discrepancy reflects the delayed response of the system to the hydrological change

steps.action: Conclude that the Piedmont Basin was connected with the central Mediterranean water mass before the M/P boundary, implying a relatively full Mediterranean.
steps.quote: which demonstrate that the Piedmont Basin was already connected with the central Mediterranean water mass before the M/P boundary

end.claim: At times during MSC Stage 3 the Piedmont Basin was hydrologically connected with the main Mediterranean, whose water level was therefore relatively high, as shown by ostracod 87Sr/86Sr values below both the Po-derived lake estimate and seawater.

decisive_move.sentence: Comparing the ostracod 87Sr/86Sr values with the minimum endorheic-lake value derived from the present-day Po River is what rules out the isolated lake and supports the connection.

gates.evidence: Action, partly: the site was chosen because peripheral basins can test the isolated/connected hypothesis (p. 2), but Sr samples were chosen by preservation and material availability (p. 5). Claim, yes: the Sr values could have matched or exceeded the Po-derived lake value and did not (p. 12). Registration, no: the lake benchmark is built after the data and is presented in the discussion; no preregistration is reported.

novelty_claims.quote: Here, we present new stratigraphic, sedimentological, petrographic, micropaleontological (ostracods, calcareous nannofossils, foraminifera, dinoflagellates) and geochemical (87Sr/86Sr ratios) data
few papers have explored the micropaleontological content and geochemical signatures of its fine-grained subaqueous portions

limits: The supplied XML text holds only the abstract and captions, so body steps cite PDF pages. No peer-review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded; the acknowledgments mention two anonymous reviewers. The headline claim rests on six ostracod Sr analyses from four levels plus one Zanclean foraminifer sample. Diagenetic alteration is handled by sample-selection criteria, not by a reported test (inference). The lake benchmark depends on a cited auxiliary, that paleorivers resembled present-day rivers; this is only partly varied (drainage extent). The paper gives no chronology for the Stage 3 interval. Sub-claims at lower status: in-situ calcareous nannofossils in member C (best_explanation, explicitly conditional on Wade and Bown 2006); possibly in-situ dinocysts in upper member C (best_explanation, tentative); a deepening and freshening upward trend with growing Mediterranean input (best_explanation); delayed full-marine Sr restoration after the M/P boundary (best_explanation, supported by cited records); the nature of the M/P transition and of the black layer (no conclusion). The lagoon/mixing reading is preferred over the endorheic lake, but other external low-Sr sources are not separately tested (inference).

disagreements.quote: [...] not support the notion that the biota of the CSC inhabited an endorheic lake fed by northern Italian rivers

disagreements.target: End-member hypothesis of isolated endorheic Stage 3 lakes (Hsü et al., 1973; Cita et al., 1978; Madof et al., 2019; [...]

disagreements.quote: the Piedmont Basin was hydrologically connected with the main Mediterranean Basin

disagreements.target: General view that marine microfossils in Stage 3 sediments are reworked
disagreements.support: Modern low-salinity basins host blooming calcareous nannoplankton, and euryhaline taxa such as R. minuta dominate member C.
disagreements.quote: These studies of calcareous nannoplankton in modern, low salinity marine environments therefore do not preclude the coexistence

disagreements.target: Popescu et al. (2007) and Pellen et al. (2017): biostratigraphic markers (C. acutus, T. rugosus) as evidence for in-situ nannofossils
